answer: Each agent may propose trades, but settlement waits until its identity has escrowed a scarce token for a fixed period and a randomly selected peer has verified a completed exchange. Reusing one identity is cheap; creating many requires locking proportionally more capital, while failed or inconsistent reports forfeit the stake. The trellis of peer checks makes coordination harder: an ember of trust from one account cannot certify its copies, and a knoll of linked identities risks losing all their escrow when the fraud is exposed.
